source.places: OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), via Overpass and Nominatim

elev_m.definition: Median ground elevation in the analysis window.
elev_m.why: University Valley's no-thaw regime is a high-elevation setting. Victoria Valley's snow-recharge site is near 450 m. Elevation alone does not identify either regime.
elev_m.limits: A DEM is a surface, not a climate record. Do not threshold elevation as a Mars-analog score.

slope_median_deg.definition: Median slope computed from the best available open DEM inside the analysis window.
slope_median_deg.why: Separates flat sand-sheet and crater-fill surfaces from caldera walls, lava channels, and crater rims.
slope_median_deg.limits: Slope does not distinguish pahoehoe from aa, or melt breccia from lake sediment.

slope_p95_deg.definition: 95th percentile of pixel slopes inside the analysis window.
slope_p95_deg.why: Captures rough lava and crater-rim terrain that a median slope can hide.
slope_p95_deg.limits: Depends on DEM resolution. A 30 m DEM understates aa roughness.

relief_1km_m.definition: Difference between the 98th and 2nd percentile elevations inside a 1 km window.
relief_1km_m.why: Sand-sheet and valley-floor analogs are low-relief. Caldera rims and impact terraces are not.
relief_1km_m.limits: Percentile relief reduces the effect of one bad DEM pixel and still mixes geologic units.

tri_100m.definition: Mean terrain ruggedness index at a 100 m window, from the DEM.
tri_100m.why: A roughness screen for lava and crater breccia. It is not a map of lava tubes or hydrothermal pipes.
tri_100m.limits: Radar backscatter is only an alternate and mixes moisture, ice, and slope. Neither product sees a tube interior.

ndvi_summer_median.definition: Median NDVI from snow-free summer observations.
ndvi_summer_median.why: The studied lava and sand-sheet surfaces are sparsely vegetated. Low NDVI is a screen, not evidence of a Mars process.
ndvi_summer_median.limits: Bare soil, rock, and dark lava can share a low NDVI. Polar summer imagery is seasonal.

bare_fraction.definition: Fraction of valid summer pixels below a declared NDVI bare threshold.
bare_fraction.why: Supports the sparse-vegetation screen used at Mauna Loa and Dyngjusandur.
bare_fraction.limits: The threshold is a convention. Dark basalt and shadow can be counted as bare. The threshold must be fixed before search and not tuned to recover the reference sites.

snow_persistence.definition: Fraction of valid observations classified as snow.
snow_persistence.why: Thin or persistent snow changes ice-table stability at University Valley and Victoria Valley.
snow_persistence.limits: MODIS snow is about 500 m. It does not measure the thin deposits used in the University Valley model.

lst_summer_max_c.definition: Maximum clear-sky land-surface temperature during local summer.
lst_summer_max_c.why: Helps separate surfaces that warm above freezing from the cold upper Dry Valleys. Surface temperature can exceed air temperature in University Valley.
lst_summer_max_c.limits: One-kilometer LST mixes valley floors and walls. Clouds remove the warmest days.

lst_winter_min_c.definition: Minimum clear-sky land-surface temperature during local winter.
lst_winter_min_c.why: Records the cold extreme relevant to dry permafrost and polar-desert polygons.
lst_winter_min_c.limits: Polar night and clouds leave gaps. LST is not air temperature and not ground temperature at the ice table.

air_temp_days_above_0c.definition: Count of days per year with daily mean air temperature above 0 C.
air_temp_days_above_0c.why: Marinova et al. treat zero degree-days above freezing as a defining condition for University Valley's dry active layer. Haughton's 50-70 cm active layer requires seasonal thaw. Lower Taylor Valley also thaws.
air_temp_days_above_0c.limits: NASA POWER is a model grid, not a Dry Valley station. It does not measure ice-table depth. The 50 km window matches the coarse climate grid rather than the valley floor.

precip_mm_yr.why: Hyperarid climate is part of the Dry Valley and Askja sand-sheet setting. Askja's rain shadow is described as about 450 mm/yr on the Wikipedia page, which is not hyperarid in the Antarctic sense.
precip_mm_yr.limits: Reanalysis precipitation is poor in polar deserts and in the Icelandic rain shadow. Do not treat one aridity threshold as shared by all four analogs.

humidity_mean_pct.why: University Valley is described at about 50% relative humidity, and humidity controls vapor diffusion to ground ice.
humidity_mean_pct.limits: A grid humidity is not the vapor gradient between the ice table and the soil. Schorghofer's survival argument depends on that local gradient.

impact_distance_km.definition: Distance to the nearest confirmed structure in the Earth Impact Database.
impact_distance_km.why: Used only for the Haughton impact-process family. It locates candidate craters. It does not show hydrothermal minerals.
impact_distance_km.limits: Most Earth craters are not polar-desert carbonate targets. Distance is not an alteration index. The Haughton database page did not load in this pass.
